option_relations.rationale: Malignant myopericytoma is a distinct diagnosis from angiosarcoma. While both are vascular tumors, they have different cellular origins and histopathological features.
Glomus tumor is a benign tumor arising from glomus bodies, which are specialized neuromyoarterial structures. It is histologically distinct from angiosarcoma.
Myoepithelial carcinoma is a malignant tumor of myoepithelial cells, typically found in salivary glands or soft tissues. It is not related to angiosarcoma.
Atypical Myopericytoma is a variant of myopericytoma, which is a perivascular tumor. It is distinct from angiosarcoma, which is a malignant tumor of endothelial cells.
